title: First sign-up on a fresh database fails with a 500 and 'Something went wrong'
where: sign-up form (Enlist with the Chapter), fresh PostgreSQL database
steps: 1. Start the API on an empty PostgreSQL database (startup seeds user 'admin' with explicit id=1). 2. Open the site, Create an account, fill username lightkeeper_rue, email, password twice. 3. Press Create account.
expected: The account is created and I land on the Chapter Hub.
actual: Red 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' under the form. POST /api/auth/register returns 500. api.log: IntegrityError UniqueViolation duplicate key value violates unique constraint users_pkey, Key (id)=(1) already exists. The seed in backend/vtt/db.py inserts User(id=1) (and Circle(id=1)) with explicit ids without advancing users_id_seq, so the first nextval() collides. Pressing Create account a second time works (the sequence has moved on to 2). Checked with psql: only 'admin' existed, users_id_seq last_value 1. A real new install would greet its very first Lightkeeper with this. Suggest setval() on the sequences after seeding, or let the DB pick the ids; and say something friendlier than 'Something went wrong'.

title: Creating the first campaign drops the table connection once (circles_pkey collision)
where: Lightkeeper's desk, right after New campaign > Create campaign, fresh database
steps: 1. On a fresh database (seed has Circle id=1), sign up and create a campaign (The Drowned Bell, code drowned-bell). 2. Watch the desk as it opens.
expected: The desk opens connected.
actual: A dark banner across the top: 'The connection to the table dropped. Reconnecting...' with RECONNECT NOW. api.log: 'WebSocket fatal error: game_id=drowned-bell error=(psycopg2.errors.UniqueViolation) duplicate key value violates unique constraint circles_pkey' from ws/endpoint.py _serve while making the campaign's circle. It reconnected by itself about 1s later (new circle id 2) and the banner went away. Same root cause as F001 (seeded rows with explicit ids, sequence not advanced), different table and symptom: the very first campaign's very first connection crashes. psql: circles = 1 'The Order of Light' (seed), 2 'Unnamed Circle'.

title: Keyboard: pressing Next card once throws focus to the page body, so you can't page through paths by keyboard
where: Character creator, step 1 Choose Path, card stack Prev/Next buttons, 1366x768

steps: 1. On the player desk, have something in the Activity Log (mine: '[00:49] Dr. Imogen Thale has archived a journal entry.' and a pass note I sent at 00:55). 2. Open the site in a second tab (same login); it opens straight on the desk.
expected: The new tab shows the same Activity Log history (rolls, pass notes, Lightkeeper's environment lines), so a player who reloads, switches device or drops off the network can catch up on what was rolled and said.
actual: The new tab's Activity Log is a blank ruled page; the old tab still shows both entries. The log lives only in the page's memory: frontend/src/store/gameStore.js keeps activityLog: [] and appends ws 'activity_log' frames (max 50), and nothing loads history on connect (checked read-only). So a reload mid-scene wipes the record of every roll and pass note made so far. errors: none.

title: Second tab is handled cleanly: the old tab says it stopped updating and 'Use this tab' hands the desk back and forth
where: player desk, two tabs of the same login; laptop 1366x768
steps: 1. With the desk open, open the site in a second tab. 2. Look at the first tab. 3. Press 'Use this tab' there, then look at the second tab.
expected: One live desk at a time, and a clear way to pick which.
actual: The first tab gets a dark bar at the top: 'This desk is open in another tab or on another device, so this one stopped updating.' with a 'Use this tab' button (announced as a status, so a screen reader hears it). Pressing it moves the bar to the other tab, and the first tab carries on. No console errors. Only nit: with the bar showing, the Your Circle rail shrinks to nothing and the hourglass label is cut off at the bottom on 1366x768 (see F104), and the new tab's log is empty (F112).

title: Field entry with a sketch: the 'Caption (optional)' text replaces the entry title, and the title I typed is thrown away
where: player desk, Notebook > Field Notes > Log a Field Entry, with a sketch attached (tablet)
steps: 1. Notebook > Field Notes. 2. Entry Title: 'Harbour office: the second mug'. 3. Write a Markdown body. 4. Tap Sketch, draw, Add to entry. 5. Caption (optional): 'Pike's crew photograph, last summer. The gap is where the arrow points.' 6. Add entry.
expected: The entry is titled 'Harbour office: the second mug', with the sketch and its caption under it; the contents list shows my title.
actual: The entry's heading (and its title in the database and the contents list) is the caption; 'Harbour office: the second mug' appears nowhere. Read-only check: notebook_entries id 3 has title = the caption text. Source: NotebookView.jsx line ~500 passes 'uploadCaption || newEntryTitle.trim() || ...' as the title, so any caption silently wins over the title. A note-keeper loses the title they wrote, and the contents list fills with long captions instead of short titles. No console errors.

title: Unpinned private note is lost without a word when you step out to the chapter hub and back
where: player desk > Notebook > Private Notes; laptop 1366x768
steps: 1. Notebook > Private Notes. 2. Type a three-line note (mine: '## Eighth locker 🗝️ / - Pike: two mugs... / - **Ask the LK**: whose boots?'). 3. Without pressing 'Pin note', press 'Back to chapter hub'. 4. Press 'Last Played: The Drowned Bell', then Notebook > Private Notes.
expected: The draft is still there (kept per viewer, the way the Field Notes and pass-note boxes are expected to keep unsent text), or leaving asks 'Pin this note first?'.
actual: The box is empty again ('Private note' placeholder, Pin note greyed). Nothing warned me when I left. Nothing in NotebookView.jsx keeps a draft (no localStorage/sessionStorage/beforeunload; checked read-only). Also: the box is about three lines tall and shows only the last line of what you type ('- **Ask the LK**: whose boots?'); the heading and first bullet scroll out of sight. Same trip also empties the Activity Log (same cause as F112: gameStore clears activityLog on leaving the desk). errors: none.

title: A field entry with a sketch or photo is never broadcast: other desks don't get it live and the Activity Log stays silent
where: player desk, Notebook > Field Notes, Add entry with a sketch attached; backend POST /api/notebook/{id}/upload
steps: 1. On one desk, add a Field Notes entry with text only (Imogen did, 00:49). 2. On another desk, add a Field Notes entry with a sketch attached (I did, 00:56). 3. Watch the WebSocket frames ('ws') and the Activity Log on a desk that stayed open.
expected: Both entries reach every desk live (notebook_entry) and both log 'X has archived a journal entry.'
actual: Imogen's text entry arrived on my desk at 00:49:41 as notebook_entry + activity_log. My sketch entry (saved fine: notebook_entries id 3) produced no WebSocket frame at all, in or out, and no Activity Log line, not even on my own desk. Read-only source check: routers/notebook.py upload_notebook_image (line ~223) saves and returns the entry but never calls manager.broadcast_campaign, unlike add_notebook_entry (~185). So other players only see sketches and photos after they reload or reopen the notebook. Asked the table to confirm from their desks. No console errors.

title: Pass Notes: no way to pass a note to the Lightkeeper alone, I am offered as my own recipient, and '(private)' doesn't say the Lightkeeper reads it too

actual: Options are @Circle (everyone), @Cassandra "Latch" Moreau (private), @Jonah Hale (private), @Dr. Imogen Thale (private), @Edda Rook (private) - the last is me. There is no Lightkeeper entry. Read-only source check: ws/handlers/chat.py also delivers every 'private' note to the campaign channel (the Lightkeeper), which is fine at a table but the label '(private)' suggests only the named player sees it. title: Gilded choice never says what keeping the gilded die earns: 'Keep the gilded die, 3' vs 'Keep the highest regular die, 6' with no mention of the drive refresh
where: player desk, dice tray, gilded choice after rolling a gilded action with a pool of 2+ (1920x1080)

expected: The choice explains the trade, e.g. 'Keep the gilded 3 (Failure, refresh 1 Intuition)' / 'Keep the 6 (Full success)', with a hover/visible line for sighted users. The whole point of a gilded die is that keeping it refreshes a drive point (the server does exactly that: handle_resolve_gilded adds 1 to the action's drive, and Well-Read would also refund my spent Intuition on a 3), but nothing on screen says so, and the slip shows no outcome for either option.
actual: Only 'KEEP ONE DIE' on the slip and two buttons named 'Keep the gilded die, 3' / 'Keep the highest regular die, 6' (screen reader). Checked the source read-only: DiceTray.jsx has no refresh wording anywhere. errors: none.

title: Patch Up is offered as a free rider on every Focus roll, so an investigation roll doubles as a healing roll
where: player desk, 'After the roll' panel under the dice tray (Doctor with Patch Up)
steps: 1. As a Doctor, roll Focus for anything that is not healing (here: reading the crew photograph while the bell rings, the Lightkeeper's call). 2. Keep the 6 (Success). 3. expected: Rulebook p. 30, Patch Up: 'When you have a few moments of calm, you can make a Focus roll to heal 1 Body mark on an ally.' actual: Any Focus roll, mid-crisis included, is followed by an offer to also heal an ally for 1 or 2 Intuition, so one roll gets both its investigative result and a heal. The ability text on the sheet has no button of its own; the only way to use it is this after-the-fact rider (usePostRollPrompts.js offers it whenever lastRoll.action is Focus/'read', read-only check of the source).
